title: THE LESSON I LEARNED FROM MARY OF BETHANY
paragraphs: THE LESSON I LEARNED FROM MARY OF BETHANY
Some people are remembered for what they built.
Some are remembered for what they conquered.
Some are remembered for what they owned.
Mary of Bethany is remembered for what she poured out.
And that may be one of the most important lessons a follower of Jesus Christ will ever learn.
Because the Kingdom of God has never measured greatness the way the world does.
The world asks what you gained.
The world counts success by what remains in your hands.
Jesus often reveals devotion by what you are willing to release.
Mary understood that before most people around her did.
And perhaps that is why her story still reaches across centuries and grips hearts today.
Because if we are honest, most of us see ourselves somewhere in that room.
But in the tension between what Jesus is worth and what we are afraid to surrender.
The story unfolds in Bethany, a village near Jerusalem.
"Then Jesus six days before the Passover came to Bethany..." (John 12:1)
It was the home of three siblings:
A family that had already experienced scandal turned into grace.
Yet Jesus stood before the tomb and called him out.
The same voice that spoke creation into existence spoke life back into a grave.
Everything had already changed for this family.
They knew something many religious people still struggle to understand.
Jesus is not merely a teacher.

ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἀνάστασις καὶ ἡ ζωή
(Egō eimi hē anastasis kai hē zōē)
"I am the resurrection and the life."
Because when Jesus enters a story, death is no longer the final chapter.
Scandal is no longer the final chapter.
Failure is no longer the final chapter.
Brokenness is no longer the final chapter.
Which is exactly what our ministry has always proclaimed:
A dinner is prepared in Jesus' honor.
The atmosphere is likely filled with gratitude.
Lazarus sits alive at the table.
Yet while everyone else is enjoying the moment, Mary sees something deeper.
She recognizes something many others are missing.
She sees Jesus not merely as a guest.
"Then took Mary a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair."
The Greek phrase describing the perfume is:
Many scholars estimate its value at roughly a year's wages.
Imagine taking an entire year's income.
And pouring it out in a single act of worship.
And that is precisely why it was beautiful.
Because true worship always costs something.
King David understood this when he declared:
"I will not offer burnt offerings unto the LORD my God of that which doth cost me nothing." (2 Samuel 24:24)
"The house was filled with the odor of the ointment."
One act of devotion transformed the atmosphere of the entire room.
One surrendered life affects everyone around it.
One transformed heart affects entire families.
One believer fully devoted to Christ changes environments without saying a word.
Mary's worship became more than a moment.
"Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred pence, and given to the poor?"
At first glance, his concern sounds spiritual.
John reveals Judas was not concerned about the poor.
How often does the flesh disguise selfishness as wisdom?
How often do people criticize extravagant devotion because they cannot understand it?
The world understands obsession with careers.
But wholehearted devotion to Jesus often appears excessive.
Mary teaches us an uncomfortable lesson.
Those who worship deeply will often be misunderstood.
She simply remained at Jesus' feet.
Imagine hearing those words from the Savior Himself.
The King of Kings defending your worship.
The Lord of Glory protecting your devotion.
The Creator of the universe saying:
"Against the day of my burying hath she kept this."
Mary perceived something many disciples still failed to understand.
She recognized His worth while He was still physically present.
She loved Him before the crowd turned.
And perhaps that is the lesson modern believers need more than ever.
Life constantly distracts us from the one thing that matters most.
The world trains us to rush.
The same Mary appears earlier in Luke 10.
Mary is sitting at Jesus' feet.
But because intimacy comes before activity.
Being with Christ before doing for Christ.
That truth has become increasingly rare.
Fewer truly sit at His feet.
Mary reminds us that intimacy is never wasted.
Time with Jesus is never wasted.
Tears at His feet are never wasted.
Nothing poured onto Jesus is ever lost.
And then comes one of the most remarkable statements in Scripture.
"Verily I say unto you, Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached in the whole world, there shall also this, that this woman hath done, be told for a memorial of her."
Yet Jesus ensured Mary's act of worship would never be forgotten.
Not because she preached a sermon.
Not because she built a platform.
But because she loved Him extravagantly.
Perhaps someone reading this feels unseen.
Nothing offered to Christ is forgotten.
That is the lesson I learned from Mary of Bethany.
The greatest thing you can pour out is not perfume.
Placed at the feet of Jesus.
Because the moment you realize who He truly is, withholding anything begins to feel unreasonable.
Mary's story ultimately points beyond Mary.
The One who left Heaven for sinners.
The One who carried our shame.
The One who bore our judgment.
The One who died our death.
The One still transforming scandal into grace today.
The Gospel is not about good people becoming slightly better.
The Gospel is about dead people being raised to life.
The Gospel is about broken stories being rewritten by the Author Himself.
If this article stirred something in your spirit, do not let the moment pass quickly.
What have I been unwilling to place at His feet?
What perfume jar am I still protecting?
What surrender am I still postponing?
Someone in your circle may desperately need the reminder that Jesus still rewrites stories.
Supporting this work allows us to continue producing Christ-centered biblical content, discipleship resources, teachings, and Gospel outreach that point people to Jesus rather than ourselves.
What is one thing you need to place at the feet of Jesus today?
Someone else may find courage through your testimony.
Because one day, every crown, every achievement, every possession, and every earthly accomplishment will fade.
But nothing poured out for Jesus is ever wasted.
Jesus is still turning scandal into grace.
The fragrance of surrendered worship never leaves the room.
